biggest_catch: Bonus value at the maximum (estimated ~$900 for up to 60,000 Hyatt points at 1.5¢ each) minus the $95 annual fee = up to ~$805 first-year net — but only 30,000 points is a flat bonus; the other up-to-30,000 comes from elevated earning on up to $15,000 of spend, so you must actually spend to get the max; only pursue it with spending already planned.
catches: Only pursue this bonus with spending you were already going to make — manufactured or extra spending can erase the gain.
Chase 5/24 rule: you will likely be denied if you have opened 5+ personal cards (any issuer) in the past 24 months.
Applying for this card triggers a hard credit inquiry — do not apply unless you are ready for it.
This card's purchase APR is roughly 20%+; carrying a balance can wipe out the entire bonus — pay the statement balance in full every month.
Only the first 30,000 points are guaranteed with $3,000 in 3 months; the rest requires up to $15,000 in qualifying spend over 6 months.
Bonus ineligible if you have this card or received its new-cardmember bonus in the past 24 months.
You must be a legitimate business to apply — a sole proprietor applying with an SSN qualifies; the account will only be used for business purposes per the issuer's terms.
